title: Equally likely outcomes and geometric probability
terms: probability; favorable outcomes; equally likely outcomes; sampling without replacement; geometric probability; uniform distribution.

exposition.text:
For a finite sample space with equally likely elementary outcomes, P (A) = |A|/|S|. The equal-
likelihood hypothesis matters: unordered dice sums, for example, are not equally likely. Sam-
pling without replacement changes the available population after each draw and naturally leads
to combinations or conditional products.
For a point chosen uniformly from a region, probability is the measure of the favorable subre-
gion divided by the total measure. Two independent uniform coordinates in [0, 1] give uniform
area on the unit square. Curved constraints become integration problems; independence and
uniformity must be specified rather than inferred from the phrase at random.

question.text:
First choose K uniformly from {1, 2, 3}. Given K = k, choose X uniformly from {1, . . . , k}.
What is P(X = 1)?
(A) 1/3 (B) 1/2 (C) 5/9 (D) 11/18 (E) 2/3

solution.text:
Partition according to the first choice. The three paths to X = 1 have probabilities 1/3,
(1/3)(1/2), and (1/3)(1/3). Their sum is 1/3 + 1/6 + 1/9 = 11/18. Although both steps are
individually uniform on their allowed choices, the final values 1, 2, 3 are not equally likely.
